facts.raw_span: A 55-year-old man
history of coronary artery disease status post–bypass surgery
emphysema
chest pain, dyspnea, cough, night sweats, and a 20-pound unintentional weight loss
Physical examination was unremarkable
Laboratory studies, including a complete blood count and comprehensive metabolic profile, were within normal limits
a retrocardiac necrotic mediastinal mass measuring 1.2 × 8.6 × 10.7 cm
causing mass effect on the esophagus, left atrium, and pulmonary veins
Transbronchial needle aspiration of a right hilar mass showed benign bronchial cells
EUS-guided FNA of an oval, hypoechoic posterior mediastinal lesion (68 × 70 mm) obtained a core biopsy that demonstrated a spindle cell neoplasm with large nuclei and prominent nucleoli
Immunohistochemical staining was positive for CD117, DOG1, Cam5.2, and AE1/AE3
Somatic genetic analysis of cKIT and PDGFRA revealed no mutations, and germline testing was positive for NF1, suggesting wild-type GIST

concepts.why: The presence of a spindle cell neoplasm with large nuclei and prominent nucleoli, positive immunohistochemical staining for CD117, DOG1, Cam5.2, and AE1/AE3, and somatic genetic analysis suggesting wild-type GIST support this diagnosis.
The presence of multiple pulmonary nodules, hilar lymph nodes, and a pleural-based lesion on PET imaging, in addition to the primary mediastinal mass, suggests metastatic disease.
The mediastinal mass is causing mass effect on the esophagus, left atrium, and pulmonary veins, which is a characteristic finding in mediastinal GIST.

rationales.F07: The presence of a retrocardiac necrotic mediastinal mass suggests a possible mediastinal GIST.
rationales.F08: The mass effect on the esophagus, left atrium, and pulmonary veins is consistent with a mediastinal GIST.
rationales.F10: The core biopsy demonstrating a spindle cell neoplasm with large nuclei and prominent nucleoli is consistent with GIST.
rationales.F11: The positive immunohistochemical staining for CD117, DOG1, Cam5.2, and AE1/AE3 supports the diagnosis of GIST.
rationales.F12: The absence of cKIT and PDGFRA mutations and the presence of NF1 suggest a wild-type GIST.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of a retrocardiac necrotic mediastinal mass, multiple pulmonary nodules, hilar lymph nodes, and a pleural-based lesion on PET imaging, along with the patient's symptoms and the biopsy results, support the diagnosis of Malignant GIST with metastasis.
